title: Living walls
text: Vertical gardens, or 'living walls', are transforming city architecture. A living wall is a whole surface covered in plants, watered by {{1}} (CONCEAL) irrigation systems. Their benefits go far beyond {{2}} (APPEAR). The plants insulate buildings, cutting energy use, and their leaves trap dust and pollution, measurably improving air {{3}} (QUALIFY). In hot summers a living wall can keep a facade twenty degrees cooler, an effect that has made them {{4}} (INCREASE) popular with city planners. Maintenance, however, is demanding: systems fail if pumps break, and {{5}} (REPAIR) can be costly. The world's largest living wall, in Milan, contains over 44,000 plants and has become a tourist {{6}} (ATTRACT). Critics dismiss such projects as temporary {{7}} (FASHION), but research increasingly supports their {{8}} (EFFECT) at cooling streets and cleaning air.
